value.body: A critical care nurse works in intensive care units (ICU, CCU, NICU and similar), looking after patients who need constant monitoring and life support. Multi-speciality and tertiary hospitals hire for these units. A typical shift involves close patient monitoring, managing equipment such as ventilators and infusion pumps, giving medicines, and working alongside intensivists.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Nursing or GNM, registered with a State Nursing Council

items.label: Further training
items.value: Post-basic critical care courses often follow

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most nurses start as staff nurses on general wards and move to the ICU after some experience; some hospitals take freshers directly into ICUs with on-the-job training. Basic and advanced life-support certifications are commonly required.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: ICU charge nurse, nurse educator, critical care nurse specialist.
Rotating shifts, including nights, are standard.
ICU experience is also valued for nursing jobs abroad.
